rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent stepped bar in all four views, so it avoids total fragmentation, but the massing is too generic and internally inconsistent with the requested neighborhood-living contract. The dominant object is a stair-stepped extruded block with a central notch-like void in plan, but that void is not yet clearly a legible public threshold tied to the verified access edge. In the image set, the blue road frontage sits adjacent to the parcel yet the mass does not convincingly open or hinge toward it; the access response is more sealed/peripheral than public. The top view suggests a carved center, but the section/views do not reinforce a clear programmatic ground-to-upper hierarchy or a continuous inhabited terrace sequence. The silhouette is coherent, but it behaves more like an arbitrary stepped stack than a sectionally meaningful mixed-use bar. This is close enough to the neighborhood-active-bar language to keep the gesture, but not enough to pass program fit without a stronger public edge, clearer open-space figure, and better section logic.
